title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of an elementary derivation of the chord addition law on an elliptic curve in the Weierstrass-type form z'^2 = z0^3 + a1 z0^2 + a2 z0 + a3, with a 'Weierstrass function' ℘ : E → P^1 (z0 = ℘(z), z' = ℘'(z)). It serves the notes' aim (moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2): making the group law explicit in terms of the 2-torsion data. The next page parametrizes the curve by the branch points ξ_i of ℘, with a1 = -Σξ_i, a2 = Σξ_iξ_j, a3 = -Πξ_i.

The argument runs as follows.
1. Take x, y on E with z = -(x+y). On the previous page the collinearity condition is written as the line z' = λ z0 + μ, with λ = (x'-y')/(x0-y0) and μ = (y'x0 - x'y0)/(x0-y0).
2. Substituting this into the cubic gives the cubic equation (48): z0^3 + (a1 - λ^2) z0^2 + (a2 - 2λμ) z0 + (a3 - μ^2) = 0.
3. Its roots include x0 and y0. When the third root is distinct from them, Vieta's formula gives x0 + y0 + z0 = λ^2 - a1.
4. Hence (51): z0 = λ^2 - a1 - x0 - y0 and z' = λ z0 + μ.
5. Genericity conditions (50) are stated first: x, y ≠ 0, x ≠ y, and -(x+y) ≠ x, y, i.e. y ≠ -2x and x ≠ -2y.
6. By a 'principe de prolongement' (identity of rational functions on a dense open set), the formulas then stay valid whenever x, y ∈ E(k) \ {0} and x0 ≠ y0, i.e. y ∉ {±x}. This includes the case where the line is tangent at x or y (z = x or z = y).

This is the standard chord-and-tangent addition formula.
errors: Minor: (50) lists 'x ≠ y' but not explicitly 'x ≠ -y'. That condition is needed for x0 ≠ y0 (division by x0 - y0) and was noted on the previous page; the final sentence does state y ∉ ±x.
The extension 'par principe de prolongement' is justified because both sides are rational functions agreeing on a dense open subset of E×E. Grothendieck does not spell this out, but it is standard.

ideas.what: Explicit chord addition law for E: z'^2 = z0^3 + a1 z0^2 + a2 z0 + a3, with x(P+Q) = λ^2 - a1 - x(P) - x(Q) and the corresponding formula for the second coordinate (here giving -(P+Q))
ideas.modern_name: Chord-and-tangent group law / addition formulas on a Weierstrass cubic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Newton, Jacobi, Weierstrass; Poincaré 1901 for the rational-points version); textbook material, e.g. Silverman, Tate
ideas.where_published: Standard textbooks; not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known

ideas.what: Extending the generic formula to all pairs with ℘(x) ≠ ℘(y) by density / the principle of prolongation of identities
ideas.modern_name: Extension of rational identities from a dense open set (reducedness/separatedness argument)
ideas.where_published: General principle used in EGA, but not this specific application

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook derivation of the elliptic curve addition law via Vieta's formula, written out for the author's own use in notes on moduli in characteristic ≠ 2. Nothing new or uncredited appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '\int_0 = x_0, \int_0 = y_0' should read 'z_0 = x_0, z_0 = y_0' (the symbol is z_0; above it 'x_0' is struck out and replaced).
'{+$z$ réserve+}' is better read as an insertion 'sous réserve' (with a deleted fragment 'd'autre r...'), i.e. 'on aura encore, sous réserve que (50) ...'.
In (50) the handwriting reads '-(x+y) ≠ x, y' and '2x+y ≠ 0, 2y+x ≠ 0', as the transcription has; this is consistent.
'Par principe de prolongement' is correctly read; the next-to-last line is 'tels que y ∉ ±x' with a struck-out 'x ≠'.
